input:
If ∫₀^(1/2) x²/(1-x²)^(3/2) dx = k/6, then the value of k is

Options:
A. 2√3 - π
B. 2√3 + π
C. 3√2 + π
D. 3√2 - π

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^(1/2) x²/(1-x²)^(3/2) dx using trigonometric substitution and express it in the form k/6 to find k.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: The integrand involves (1-x²)^(3/2), which suggests the substitution x = sin θ to simplify using the identity 1-sin²θ = cos²θ.

key_formulas.substitution: x = sin θ  →  dx = cos θ dθ
key_formulas.tan_to_sec: ∫tan²θ dθ = ∫(sec²θ-1) dθ = tan θ - θ + c

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute x = sin θ, change the limits, simplify the integrand to tan²θ, integrate using sec²θ-1, and evaluate at the new limits to get I, then multiply by 6 to find k.
logical_steps: Step 1: Substitute x = sin θ, dx = cos θ dθ
Step 6: Evaluate at limits and find k
